messages.subject: Data input
parts:
Hi Murray,

 

I'm confused about how to organise my data in "secr". I'm trying to create a multi-session study to estimate hippos' population size in a natural park. The study consisted of placing six camera stations at different locations (1 camera per station) for 3 years (station 4 was only active for 2 years because the camera was stolen). In total 42 hippos were identified. The thing is, cameras were active during different months in each year (please see the photo attached). 

 

I wasn't sure how to determine the occasions, so I did this (please see 2nd photo attached). Please let me know if this is okay since I do not know if this is how I should determine occasions.

 

 

I'm assuming that:

- "Sessions" are the years of the study (2019, 2020, 2021)

-  "Occasions" are the encounters (for example. on "occasion 50" different individuals could be detected, and this means they were detected on station 6, year 2019, month September). 

- "detectors" are the camera stations (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6), and I considered it as a "count" detector (several individuals can be recorded)

 

Can you please tell me if this is right please? 

 

Also, I imported the data like this and it worked. 

 

```{r}
library(secr)
captfile <- system.file("extdata", "aidcaptdet2.csv", c("sess2019.csv", "sess2020.csv", "sess2021.csv"), package = "secr", noccasions=58)
trapfile <- system.file("extdata", "aidtraps.csv", package = "secr", noccasions=58)

captfile <- system.file("extdata", "aidcaptdet2.csv", c("sess2019.csv", "sess2020.csv", "sess2021.csv"), package = "secr")
trapfile <- system.file("extdata", "aidtraps.csv", package = "secr")
```

 

But when I try to read the capthist, this error appears: 

```{r}
library(secr)
setwd("/Users/marcelagomez/Desktop/Dissertation/Rstudio thesis")   
aidcp <- read.capthist(captfile = "aidcaptdet2.csv", c("sess2019.csv", "sess2020.csv", "sess2021.csv"), trapfile = "aidtraps.csv", 
    fmt = "XY", detector = "count", binary.usage = FALSE, skip = 1)
```

Error in array(0, dim = c(nID, nocc, ndetector(traps))) : negative length vectors are not allowed

 

Please, find attached the Excel documents with my data if you need them.

 

Apologies for so many questions, I'm new using SECR and I'm a bit confused

 

Thank you so much, I truly appreciate your help

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Data input
parts:
Hello Marcela
Your assumptions about sessions, occasions and detectors are broadly 'right,' but it seems arbitrary to split consecutive months into sessions like this. Really you need to think about the likely turnover in the population, whether an open population model is needed etc. The numbers are small, and I am dubious you really have suitable data for spatial capture-recapture given the small number of cameras (probably placed in some non-representative way), the likely aggregation of hippos etc. Could you reliably distinguish all individuals?

Regarding the code:  the system.file function is used for retrieving the names of files distributed with the package, not for your own files. Those lines don't achieve anything.
The second argument of the read.capthist function is 'trapfile'. I don't know what you intended with the vector of file names as the second argument, as you also set trapfile = "aidtraps.csv".

Sorry to be discouraging, but I do think you need to think this through a bit more. I also wish other group members were not so shy about contributing!
Murray

messages.author: ec6a8aa7c56fe7fd
messages.subject: Re: Data input
parts:
Hi Marcela,

I'm quite late to this but just sharing some experiences with long surveys and multisession models in case useful.

It sounds like your post has two parts. One is how to get this analysis to run in secr. The other is about whether a multisession approach is a good idea for your data.

I couldn't see your attachments so feel free to repost or send them offline and I can try to help with the first. The multisession vignette (https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html) is useful if you haven't seen that already. You likely do have count detectors and in that case the definition of occasion isn't important because data gets collapsed into a single occasion per session. 

About the general suitability, I've used multisession models for data similar to yours where cameras have been left out for a long time and sample sizes are small, in a similar way to what you propose. I think it can be justified but you have to pretty careful because SECR models assume that populations are closed within session and independent between sessions, and when you split up a longer survey into sessions with no gaps between sessions you almost certainly violate at least one of those assumptions.

The trade-off is that you get a bigger sample size relative to what you'd get with a single session, or sessions separated by enough time that independence is reasonable. Sometimes that makes the crucial difference between getting a model to fit at all and not. In those cases the correct response is probably that the data aren't sufficient for SECR, but that can be pretty tough to hear after a big survey effort and I've not been brave enough to try it! So I guess I see the approach you outline as a pragmatic approach to an imperfect situation. Open population models are also an option, but tricky with small samples and more complicated in general.

If you do go this route there are a bunch of related choices, like how long your sessions should be, whether you can afford to have gaps between sessions, your choice of time 'origin', and whether parameters should be session-specific or shared. The multisession vignette says confidence intervals will be too narrow, so there's also that to consider. Basically the approach isn't without issues but awareness of those issues, being able to motivate your choices of e.g session length, and running plenty of checks to see how sensitive your results are to these choices will go a long way. More generally I think it's a topic where a broader simulation study would be useful because the situation seems to come up reasonably often and there is limited guidance (perhaps because it's a bad idea).

Unrelated to the multisession stuff, six cameras (if I've read that correctly) is very few and that ultimately might make the data unsuitable for SECR. A rough guide is that you'd want enough cameras to at the very least cover an animal's typical home range with 1-2 sigma spacing between cameras. That can't be done with 6 cameras and so your ability to estimate sigma especially might be poor.

Hope that helps, good luck.

Ian

messages.author: ec6a8aa7c56fe7fd
messages.subject: Re: Data input
parts:
Sorry, saw that you did attach data... don't know how I missed that. For multisession analyses I've found it useful to make data frames with traps and capture history info and then read these into secr (there are lots of other ways). This seems to work:

> library(secr)
> library(dplyr)
> library(tidyr)
>
> # make data.frame traps_df with Session column (same traps each session except 2021)
> traps_df <- read.csv("data/aidtraps.csv") %>% rename(Detector = DetectorID, x = X, y = Y)
> traps_df <- rbind(traps_df, traps_df, traps_df) %>% mutate(Session = rep(c(2019, 2020, 2021), each = 6))
> traps_df <- traps_df %>% filter(!((Session == 2021) & (Detector == "S4")))
>
> # make data.frame ch_df with Session column
> ch_df <- read.csv("data/aidcaptdet2.csv") %>%
+   mutate(Occasion = 1) %>%
+   dplyr::select(Session, Animal.ID, Occasion, Detector) %>% as.data.frame()
>
> traps_ms <- list()
> session_names <- c(2019, 2020, 2021)
> for(i in 1:length(unique(traps_df$Session))){
+   tmp <- traps_df %>% dplyr::filter(Session == session_names[i]) %>% dplyr::select(Detector, x, y)
+   traps_ms[[i]] <- read.traps(data = tmp, detector = "count", trapID = "Detector")
+ }
>
> capthist_ms <- make.capthist(captures = ch_df, traps = traps_ms)
> verify(capthist_ms)
No errors found :-)
> summary(capthist_ms, terse = TRUE)
           2019 2020 2021
Occasions     1    1    1
Detections  164  335  226
Animals      11   17   21
Detectors     6    6    5
